headline: Graph-based models of cell-cell interactions and gene regulation in single-cell data
label: Single Cell Spatial Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Spatial and multiome single-cell data now support graph models of condition-specific crosstalk, multi-scale interactions, and regulatory networks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of intercellular and regulatory relationships from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, increasingly framed on graphs. Bilinear edge classification compares spatial omics graphs across conditions to detect condition-specific crosstalk, and InterScale uses a graph-transformer to model multi-scale cell-cell interactions. MERFISH with Cellouette segmentation resolves cardiomyocyte states and microenvironments across more than 400,000 cells in the pressure-overloaded heart, and pyTrance predicts subcellular RNA co-localization from spatial data. Other items address perturbation-response and regulatory modeling, including PEPR-GNN, D-SPIN, and PRIM, alongside representation, transfer, and annotation work such as CAPTAIN, MUSE, scHG, and ScNucAdapt. What is new is the emphasis on relationships defined by niche, condition, or cell state. The set is heterogeneous, so this thread describes the dominant direction rather than a shared method.
